pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Dark brown patches exhibit high edge angularity with irregular, jagged borders and multi-lobed geometries. Patch size is heterogeneous, featuring large, sprawling regions on the mid-neck and smaller, more compact polygonal shapes on the posterior flank.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: The light-colored pelage forms a continuous, high-contrast topological network of narrow pathways. Junction nodes are predominantly three-way intersections, with pathway thickness remaining relatively consistent throughout the mid-flank and neck regions.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane presents a continuous, low-amplitude, high-frequency serrated silhouette against the blurred background along the upper neck and shoulder ridge.

other_distinctive_markers: Presence of multiple symbiotic oxpecker birds (Buphagus sp.) perched on the animal, specifically one prominent individual on the posterior rump and another partially visible on the upper neck mane.
